hypotheses.justification: The theorem also takes `[T2Space X]` from the same `variable` line. Mathlib has the instance `T2Space.t1Space`, so a `T1Space X` instance follows from `[T2Space X]`. `injG` does take a `T1Space X` instance: it comes in through `ψVOf`, whose body uses `restrict_ψ_mem_linSysOn` (stated with only `omit [ConnectedSpace X] in`), and through `cleanNbhd`/`exists_clean_nhds`. If the theorem drops `[T1Space X]` (e.g. `omit [ConnectedSpace X] [T1Space X] in`), instance search fills that argument of `injG` from the T2 instance, so the statement still elaborates. `T1Space` is a `Prop`-valued class, so by proof irrelevance the resulting statement is definitionally the same as the original. The proof is unchanged: it only unfolds `injG` with `change` to the `dite` and closes it with `dite_eq_right` and `hnot`, and nothing in it uses the T1 instance specifically. This is the same pattern as `[Nonempty α]` next to `[Inhabited α]`.
